issue.title: [Bug] Portable VS Code 能被识别，但使用了错误的 %APPDATA%\Code\User 数据目录
issue.body:
## 问题概述

通过 Scoop 安装 VS Code 后，Magpie 能识别到 VS Code，但使用的是普通安装方式的数据目录：

```text
%APPDATA%\Code\User
```

该目录实际上不存在。Scoop 版 VS Code 使用 portable data 布局，真实目录是：

```text
%SCOOP%\apps\vscode\current\data\user-data\User
```

因此 Magpie 虽然显示了 VS Code，但对 VS Code 的 provider、模型和 `settings.json` 的修改不会作用到实际运行的 VS Code。

## 环境

- Magpie: `0.1.1319`
- VS Code: `1.143.0`
- 安装方式: `scoop install vscode`

## 行为

Magpie 把 VS Code 标记为已安装，但 `Agent.Dir` 和 `Agent.Path` 仍然指向固定计算出的：

```text
%APPDATA%\Code\User
```

即使该目录不存在，PATH 中存在 `code.cmd` 也足以让检测成功。随后对 `settings.json`、`chatLanguageModels.json` 和 profiles 的读写都发生在错误目录中，实际运行的 Scoop 版 VS Code 看不到这些配置。

10 月 23 日的验证记录：新增回归在旧实现下失败，涵盖 Stable、Insiders、VSCodium；connect/sync/disconnect、链接 launcher、显式 portable 数据和普通安装边界通过，agent/agentenv 定向 race 检查通过三轮。组合验证提交 [348fb7567a74e605e535f07a208fe966b633b45b](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/348fb7567a74e605e535f07a208fe966b633b45b) 记录了 Go 1.26.8、隔离 HOME 下 native/Linux nogui/Windows vet 和 build，以及组合树的完整 Go 测试通过。这些是原交付时的验证记录，本次没有重新宣称全套运行。

2026-10-26 复查：旧提交与远端分支仍可访问；本轮再次实现了同一问题，属于重复劳动，已撤回其“新交付”计数，仍以上面的原分支为准。

未验证限制：没有真实 Windows/Scoop 或 macOS 编辑器运行；交叉编译不等于平台运行验证。

## Summary

Scoop's VS Code is a portable build: it was detected, but magpie's `Agent.Dir` stayed at `%APPDATA%\Code\User`, which doesn't exist — `code.cmd` on PATH was detection enough — so the provider, models and `settings.json` magpie wrote went where the build never reads. A portable build's User folder is in its data folder: `data\user-data\User` beside the program.

## Root cause

`vscodeUserDir` (internal/agent/vscode.go) always computed the OS's place for the User folder, `%APPDATA%` on Windows; only detection ever looked at the editor itself, by its launcher alone (`proc.Look` in the agent's `detect`). So any portable build — a zip with its `data` folder beside it, or Scoop's, whose `apps\vscode\current\data` is the persisted one — was found and then read and written in a folder it doesn't use.

## Fix

A build whose launcher has a `data` folder beside it is portable, as VS Code itself takes a build for portable by that folder alone: its User folder is `data\user-data\User` there, where it is found, wired, connected and disconnected. The launcher is found as detection finds it, and a Scoop shim stands for the launcher the `.shim` beside it names (`path = ...`), which `proc.Unwrap` doesn't read. Zoo Code, which keeps its settings in VS Code's User folder, is laid out by the same function and follows it.

An installed build's launcher has no data folder beside it and keeps the OS's place; so does a portable build before its first run, whose launcher alone is still detection enough, its writes then making the folder where it reads. VSCodium portable is left as it was: its data folder is named by its product.json, which no report asks after.

## Verification

| `go test -race ./internal/agent -run TestVSCodePortable -count=1` | pass |
| `go test -tags nogui ./internal/agent -count=1` | green but TestMothX, which fails the same on 0c679c64 — this Mac's PATH has a real `mothx` (fnm), which that test's LookPath finds |
| `go test -tags nogui ./internal/library -count=1` (a consumer of Detected) | pass |
| `gofmt -l internal/agent` | clean |
| `go vet` darwin, `GOOS=linux -tags nogui`, `GOOS=windows` (tests included) | pass |
| `go build` darwin, `GOOS=linux -tags nogui`, `GOOS=windows` | pass |
| `GOOS=windows go test -c -o /dev/null ./internal/agent` | windows tests compile; not run — this was written and verified on a Mac |

+package agent
+
+import (
+	"os"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"runtime"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/tidwall/gjson"
+	"github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/edit"
+)
+
+// portableVSCode lays VS Code out under home as a portable build is: its
+// launcher in bin, and, when portable, its data folder beside the program —
+// a zip's own, or Scoop's, whose apps\vscode\current\data is the persisted
+// one (current a junction into apps\vscode, which a folder reads through
+// the same). The launcher is put on PATH; with shims, a Scoop shim of it
+// is, as scoop's shims folder has.
+func portableVSCode(t *testing.T, home string, portable, shims bool) (user string) {
+	t.Helper()
+	app := filepath.Join(home, "Editor With Spaces")
+	binDir := filepath.Join(app, "bin")
+	if shims {
+		app = filepath.Join(home, "scoop", "apps", "vscode", "current")
+		binDir = filepath.Join(home, "scoop", "shims")
+	}
+	name := "code"
+	if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
+		name += ".cmd"
+		t.Setenv("PATHEXT", ".CMD")
+	}
+	writeAt(t, filepath.Join(app, "bin", name), "launcher\n")
+	if err := os.Chmod(filepath.Join(app, "bin", name), 0o755); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if shims {
+		writeAt(t, filepath.Join(binDir, name), "shim\n")
+		if err := os.Chmod(filepath.Join(binDir, name), 0o755); err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+		writeAt(t, filepath.Join(binDir, "code.shim"), "path = "+filepath.Join(app, "bin", name)+"\n")
+	}
+	if portable {
+		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(app, "data"), 0o755); err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+		user = filepath.Join(app, "data", "user-data", "User")
+	}
+	t.Setenv("PATH", binDir)
+	return user
+}
+
+// installedUserDir is the User folder of an installed VS Code, where the OS
+// puts it.
+func installedUserDir(home string) string {
+	switch runtime.GOOS {
+	case "windows":
+		return filepath.Join(os.Getenv("APPDATA"), "Code", "User")
+	case "darwin":
+		return filepath.Join(home, "Library", "Application Support", "Code", "User")
+	}
+	return filepath.Join(os.Getenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME"), "Code", "User")
+}
+
+// YOUIMARK's Windows has Scoop's VS Code, a portable build: magpie showed
+// the editor, but its Dir stayed %APPDATA%\Code\User, which doesn't exist —
+// code.cmd on PATH was detection enough — so its provider, models and
+// settings.json went where the build never reads (#3260). A portable
+// build's User folder is in its data folder: data\user-data\User beside the
+// program. An installed build, whose launcher has no data folder beside it,
+// keeps the OS's.
+func TestVSCodePortableUserDir(t *testing.T) {
+	home, cfg := syncHome(t), os.Getenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
+	// the launcher is taken through filepath.EvalSymlinks, which a Mac's
+	// temporary folders come out of one symlink longer
+	if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(home); err == nil {
+		home = resolved
+	}
+	portableVSCode(t, home, false, false)
+	if a := vscode(home, cfg); a.Dir != installedUserDir(home) {
+		t.Fatalf("an installed build's User folder is %s, want %s", a.Dir, installedUserDir(home))
+	}
+	user := portableVSCode(t, home, true, false)
+	a := vscode(home, cfg)
+	if a.Dir != user {
+		t.Fatalf("the portable build's User folder is %s, want %s", a.Dir, user)
+	}
+	// before its first run has made the folder, its launcher alone is
+	// detection enough — and connecting writes there, where it reads
+	if !a.Detected() {
+		t.Fatal("the portable build isn't listed")
+	}
+	if err := a.Connect(); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	lm := filepath.Join(a.Dir, "chatLanguageModels.json")
+	if g, ok := edit.GetJSONItem(lm, vscodeGroup); !ok || gjson.Get(g, "models.0.id").String() != "relay/glm-4.6" {
+		t.Fatalf("not wired in the data folder:\n%s", readFile(lm))
+	}
+	if err := a.Disconnect(); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if _, ok := edit.GetJSONItem(lm, vscodeGroup); ok {
+		t.Fatalf("disconnected, magpie's group kept:\n%s", readFile(lm))
+	}
+}
+
+// Scoop's code.cmd is a shim: the launcher it stands for is named by the
+// .shim beside it (proc.Unwrap doesn't read those), and the data folder is
+// the persisted one. A shim of a launcher with no data folder beside it is
+// an installed build; its steps run in that order, as a data folder made
+// stays.
+func TestVSCodePortableScoopShim(t *testing.T) {
+	home, cfg := syncHome(t), os.Getenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
+	if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(home); err == nil {
+		home = resolved
+	}
+	portableVSCode(t, home, false, true)
+	if a := vscode(home, cfg); a.Dir != installedUserDir(home) {
+		t.Fatalf("an installed build's User folder is %s, want %s", a.Dir, installedUserDir(home))
+	}
+	user := portableVSCode(t, home, true, true)
+	if a := vscode(home, cfg); a.Dir != user {
+		t.Fatalf("Scoop's portable VS Code reads %s, want %s", a.Dir, user)
+	}
+}

Scoop's VS Code is a portable build: it was detected, but magpie's `Agent.Dir` stayed at `%APPDATA%\Code\User`, which doesn't exist — `code.cmd` on PATH was detection enough — so the provider, models and `settings.json` magpie wrote went where the build never reads. +// launcher in bin, and, when portable, its data folder beside the program —
+// a zip's own, or Scoop's, whose apps\vscode\current\data is the persisted
+// one (current a junction into apps\vscode, which a folder reads through
+// the same). The launcher is put on PATH; with shims, a Scoop shim of it
+// is, as scoop's shims folder has.
+func portableVSCode(t *testing.T, home string, portable, shims bool) (user string) {
+	t.Helper()
+	app := filepath.Join(home, "Editor With Spaces")
+	binDir := filepath.Join(app, "bin")
+	if shims {
+		app = filepath.Join(home, "scoop", "apps", "vscode", "current")
+		binDir = filepath.Join(home, "scoop", "shims")
+	}
+	name := "code"
+	if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
+		name += ".cmd"
+		t.Setenv("PATHEXT", ".CMD")
+	}
+	writeAt(t, filepath.Join(app, "bin", name), "launcher\n")
+	if err := os.Chmod(filepath.Join(app, "bin", name), 0o755); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if shims {
+		writeAt(t, filepath.Join(binDir, name), "shim\n")
+		if err := os.Chmod(filepath.Join(binDir, name), 0o755); err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+		writeAt(t, filepath.Join(binDir, "code.shim"), "path = "+filepath.Join(app, "bin", name)+"\n")
+	}
+	if portable {
+		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(app, "data"), 0o755); err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+		user = filepath.Join(app, "data", "user-data", "User")
+	}

+}
+
+// installedUserDir is the User folder of an installed VS Code, where the OS
+// puts it.
+func installedUserDir(home string) string {
+	switch runtime.GOOS {
+	case "windows":

+	case "darwin":

+// YOUIMARK's Windows has Scoop's VS Code, a portable build: magpie showed
+// the editor, but its Dir stayed %APPDATA%\Code\User, which doesn't exist —
+// code.cmd on PATH was detection enough — so its provider, models and
+// settings.json went where the build never reads (#3260). A portable
+// build's User folder is in its data folder: data\user-data\User beside the
+// program. An installed build, whose launcher has no data folder beside it,
+// keeps the OS's.
+func TestVSCodePortableUserDir(t *testing.T) {
+	home, cfg := syncHome(t), os.Getenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")

+	// temporary folders come out of one symlink longer
+	if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(home); err == nil {
+		home = resolved
+	}
+	portableVSCode(t, home, false, false)
+	if a := vscode(home, cfg); a.Dir != installedUserDir(home) {
+		t.Fatalf("an installed build's User folder is %s, want %s", a.Dir, installedUserDir(home))
+	}
+	user := portableVSCode(t, home, true, false)
+	a := vscode(home, cfg)
+	if a.Dir != user {
+		t.Fatalf("the portable build's User folder is %s, want %s", a.Dir, user)
+	}
+	// before its first run has made the folder, its launcher alone is
+	// detection enough — and connecting writes there, where it reads
+	if !a.Detected() {
+		t.Fatal("the portable build isn't listed")
+	}
+	if err := a.Connect(); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	lm := filepath.Join(a.Dir, "chatLanguageModels.json")
+	if g, ok := edit.GetJSONItem(lm, vscodeGroup); !ok || gjson.Get(g, "models.0.id").String() != "relay/glm-4.6" {
+		t.Fatalf("not wired in the data folder:\n%s", readFile(lm))
+	}
+	if err := a.Disconnect(); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if _, ok := edit.GetJSONItem(lm, vscodeGroup); ok {
+		t.Fatalf("disconnected, magpie's group kept:\n%s", readFile(lm))
+	}
+}
+
+// Scoop's code.cmd is a shim: the launcher it stands for is named by the
+// .shim beside it (proc.Unwrap doesn't read those), and the data folder is
+// the persisted one. A shim of a launcher with no data folder beside it is
+// an installed build; its steps run in that order, as a data folder made
+// stays.
+func TestVSCodePortableScoopShim(t *testing.T) {
+	home, cfg := syncHome(t), os.Getenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
+	if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(home); err == nil {
+		home = resolved
+	}
+	portableVSCode(t, home, false, true)
+	if a := vscode(home, cfg); a.Dir != installedUserDir(home) {
+		t.Fatalf("an installed build's User folder is %s, want %s", a.Dir, installedUserDir(home))
+	}
+	user := portableVSCode(t, home, true, true)
+	if a := vscode(home, cfg); a.Dir != user {

issue.title: Windows: VS Code's bundled copilot launcher shim makes Magpie report Copilot CLI as installed

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Summary

On Windows, `magpie ls` and `magpie agents` report **Copilot CLI as detected** even though the CLI was never installed and `~\.copilot` does not exist. The false positive comes from the `copilot` launcher shim that **VS Code 1.143.0 ships in its `bin` folder**, which VS Code puts on the user's registry `PATH`. Magpie's `Detected()` sees a `copilot` executable there and treats it as the CLI.

The same entry also shows up in the Library / shared-instructions agent list as a writable target (`~\.copilot\copilot-instructions.md`).

## Environment

- magpie **0.1.1320** (Windows x64)
- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200
- VS Code **1.143.0** (commit `2d0b7506a36c1d6db9a466440131a8e01eab2289`), installed under `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code`
- Shell: Git Bash

## Reproduction

1. Copilot CLI is not installed:
   - `C:\Users\<user>\.copilot` does not exist.
   - `copilot --version` prints:
     ```
     GitHub Copilot CLI was not found. Run copilot in a terminal to install it, or see
     https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/set-up-copilot-cli/install-copilot-cli
     ```
2. The `copilot` command on PATH is VS Code's launcher, not the CLI:
   ```
   > where copilot
   C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\bin\copilot-shim\copilot
   C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\bin\copilot-shim\copilot.exe
   ```
   The shim identifies itself as `vscode-copilot-launcher`; the files were written by the VS Code update (2026-10-20).
   The user's registry PATH contains both `...\Microsoft VS Code\bin` and `...\Microsoft VS Code\bin\copilot-shim`.
3. Magpie reports it as detected:
   ```
   > magpie ls
     ...
     Copilot CLI      —  ·  effort —       ~\.copilot\settings.json
   ```
   `magpie agents` shows `Copilot CLI` with its config path, while other absent agents (Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, …) show `not detected`.
4. Renaming `...\Microsoft VS Code\bin\copilot-shim` makes `Copilot CLI` disappear from `magpie ls`; renaming it back makes it reappear.

## Root cause

In `internal/agent/agent.go`, `(*Agent).Detected()` (line ~340) falls back to:

```go
if a.Bin != "" && binAt(a.Bin) != "" {
    return true
}
```

For Copilot CLI (`internal/agent/agents.go`, line ~1367) `Bin: "copilot"`. On Windows, `binAt` falls back to `proc.FindTool`, which falls back to the **registry PATH** (`proc.LoginPath`) and known tool folders. VS Code's launcher shim is found there, so the agent is marked installed.

Note that the agent already sets `dirShared: true` with the comment that JetBrains/VS Code plugins write `~/.copilot` and the folder says nothing about the CLI (#1495) — but the `Bin` lookup has no equivalent guard for VS Code's launcher.

## Suggested fix

Any one of these would remove the false positive:

1. Ignore a `copilot` binary located under VS Code's `bin\copilot-shim` directory (or under a VS Code `bin` in general) in `Detected()` / a copilot-specific `detect`.
2. Verify the found binary is the real CLI (e.g. run `copilot --version` and reject the launcher's "GitHub Copilot CLI was not found" output).
3. For this agent, require `~\.copilot\settings.json` and treat `Bin`-only detection as not installed.

Related but different: #1495 (residual config directories counted as installed).

issue.title: [Bug][macOS] 便携版 VS Code 已识别，但配置仍写入默认目录，忽略 code-portable-data

repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## 问题

macOS 便携版 VS Code 可以被 Magpie 识别，界面显示“已接入”，但 Magpie 修改的是普通安装的用户配置目录。实际运行的便携版读取另一处目录，因此无法收到这些模型配置。

相关 Windows 报告：#3260、#4009。本 Issue 补充 macOS 的实际安装布局及可直接解析的启动器软链接。

## 环境与实际路径

- 操作系统：macOS。
- 编辑器：VS Code Stable，使用官方 Portable Mode。
- Magpie 和 VS Code 的具体版本号尚未提供。
- 源码定位基线：`3142a555945d85b73591c791690d998809a0d72f`。

应用和数据目录：

```text
/Applications/Code/
├── Visual Studio Code.app
└── code-portable-data/
    ├── user-data/User/
    └── extensions/
```

终端实际输出：

```text
❯ which code
/usr/local/bin/code

❯ ls -l /usr/local/bin/code
lrwxr-xr-x 1 root wheel 73 Mar  6  2025 /usr/local/bin/code -> '/Applications/Code/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/bin/code'
```

启动器已经在 PATH 中，且软链接明确指向这份便携安装。

## 复现步骤

1. 按上述布局在 macOS 配置便携版 VS Code。
2. 将 `code` 命令加入 PATH，确认软链接指向该应用。
3. 在 Magpie 中启用 VS Code Chat 集成并选择模型。
4. 查看 Magpie 界面显示的修改路径，以及便携目录下的配置文件。
5. 打开便携版 VS Code，新建 Chat 会话检查模型列表。

## 实际结果

Magpie 显示“已接入”，但界面明确显示修改了：

```text
~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/settings.json
~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/chatLanguageModels.json
```

便携版实际读取：

```text
/Applications/Code/code-portable-data/user-data/User/settings.json
/Applications/Code/code-portable-data/user-data/User/chatLanguageModels.json
```

应用检测成功，配置目录却仍然使用普通安装路径。

## 源码定位

[`internal/agent/vscode.go`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/3142a555945d85b73591c791690d998809a0d72f/internal/agent/vscode.go) 中，`vscodeUserDir()` 的 macOS 分支直接拼接 `~/Library/Application Support/<folder>/User`，没有根据实际应用路径检查便携目录。

同文件中的 `vscodeCodeBinary()` 已使用 `filepath.EvalSymlinks()`，但解析结果只用于判断编辑器身份，没有参与配置目录定位。

VS Code 自身的 [`configurePortable()`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/bootstrap-node.ts) 在 macOS 上使用 `.app` 同级的 `product.portable`，或默认的 `applicationName + "-portable-data"`。官方说明：[Portable mode](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/portable)。

## 建议修复与验收

- 解析 `code` / `code-insiders` 的真实启动器路径，找到实际应用 bundle；无需启动编辑器。
- 根据该安装的 `product.json` 检查同级便携数据目录，使用其中的 `user-data/User` 与 `extensions`。
- 让模型配置、Profiles、同步、断开还原和共用这些目录的 Zoo Code 使用一致的解析结果。
- 标准安装保持原路径；多个安装并存时，其他便携副本不应接管已明确定位的普通安装。
- 覆盖包含空格的路径、单层及多层软链接、Stable / Insiders、缺少便携目录和无启动器的安装发现。
- 检查断开预览的隔离：预览子进程保留原 PATH 时，不能沿启动器重新定位并修改真实便携配置。

已在 Linux 临时目录中构造上述 macOS 布局验证候选修复：相关 VS Code / Zoo Code 测试及便携路径竞态检查通过；关闭便携解析后，回归测试会重新写入默认路径并失败。真实 macOS 图形应用的端到端验证仍待完成。


## 完整修复补丁

以下为完整的 `git format-patch` 补丁，包含实现、回归测试和子系统文档，可展开后将代码块完整保存为 `macos-vscode-portable.patch`，在仓库内通过 `git am /path/to/macos-vscode-portable.patch` 应用。

- 全量无界面测试运行完成，20 个失败测试也全部在未修改基线上复现：涉及当前测试环境的 Unix 套接字及进程检查限制，以及已有脚本体积问题 #4133。Linux 图形构建缺少 pkg-config。

+// vscodeMacPortable follows the launcher before looking in the usual app
+// folders: a code symlink can name a portable install on an external drive.
+// A known launcher also prevents another install from taking its settings.
+func vscodeMacPortable(k vscodeKind) string {
+	if bin, err := proc.Look(k.bin); err == nil {
+		if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(bin); err == nil {
+			app := filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(resolved), "..", "..", "..", ".."))
+			if strings.HasSuffix(app, ".app") && resolved == filepath.Join(app, "Contents", "Resources", "app", "bin", k.bin) {
+				return vscodePortableAt(k, app)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	var app desktopApp
+	switch k.id {
+	case vscodeStable.id:
+		app = desktopApp{id: "com.microsoft.VSCode", names: []string{"Visual Studio Code.app"}}
+	case vscodeInsiders.id:
+		app = desktopApp{id: "com.microsoft.VSCodeInsiders", names: []string{"Visual Studio Code - Insiders.app"}}
+	default:
+		return ""
+	}
+	for _, bundle := range macBundles(app) {
+		if data := vscodePortableAt(k, bundle); data != "" {
+			return data
+		}
+	}
+	return ""

+// vscodePortableAt follows VS Code's configurePortable (bootstrap-node.ts):
+// product.portable, or applicationName + "-portable-data", beside the bundle.
+// An unreadable product or another editor is not enough to redirect writes.
+func vscodePortableAt(k vscodeKind, bundle string) string {
+	b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(bundle, "Contents", "Resources", "app", "product.json"))
+	var product struct {
+		ApplicationName string          `json:"applicationName"`
+		Portable        string          `json:"portable"`
+		Target          json.RawMessage `json:"target"`
+	}
+	if err != nil || json.Unmarshal(b, &product) != nil || product.ApplicationName != k.bin || product.Target != nil {
+		return ""
+	}
+	name := product.Portable
+	if name == "" {
+		name = product.ApplicationName + "-portable-data"
+	}
+	// Only a sibling data folder can be discovered through product metadata.
+	if name == "." || name == ".." || filepath.Base(name) != name || strings.ContainsAny(name, `/\`) {
+		return ""
+	}
+	data := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(bundle), name)
+	if !isDir(data) {
+		return ""
+	}
+	return data
+}
